entries.0139b3d4cf03f5ed: This segment covers the manufacture and sale of products other than the five businesses above, and the sale and leasing of real estate. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥18,204 million, down from ¥22,286 million in the prior year (restated). This is a reportable segment, and it is listed last because its revenue is the smallest.
entries.17e48ae7284190a7: A business that makes and sells machine tools and industrial sewing machines. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥82,969 million, an increase of 23.3% from the prior year (after reclassification). Industrial equipment centered on machine tools grew significantly on expanded capital investment in automotive and general machinery in China and Asia, while industrial sewing machines declined as capital investment for apparel in Asia was sluggish due to the effects of U.S. tariff policy. The company began machine tool production at its Indian subsidiary in December 2024, and in January 2026 acquired the automotive parts division of Germany's Konrad Busche, strengthening the non-apparel field of industrial sewing machines, such as automotive interior parts.
entries.2819558f1f17641c: Machine bodies such as laser multifunction machines, printers and inkjet multifunction machines, and their consumables. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥498,348 million (up 4.8% from the prior year).
entries.2d9946761bf5cbb9: This business has manufactured, sold and leased the commercial networked karaoke equipment “JOYSOUND” and provided content services, and it is carried out by Exing Co., Ltd. From the fiscal year ended March 2026, it has been classified as a discontinued operation, and because it is not included in reportable segment revenue, the amount of this business’s revenue is not printed in the segment information. In November 2025, the karaoke store business and other operations of Standard Co., Ltd. were transferred to Koshidaka Holdings Co., Ltd., and on April 1, 2026, 70% of Exing’s shares were transferred to U-NEXT HOLDINGS Co., Ltd., so Exing and its subsidiaries ceased to be consolidated subsidiaries.
entries.57073533232c67b0: A business centered on Domino Printing Sciences in the United Kingdom, providing sales of various coding and marking equipment through to after-sales service. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥125,326 million (up 5.0% from the prior year).
entries.8bc4da3dc3cbce91: A machinery manufacturer that makes printers, multifunction machines, sewing machines, machine tools and more, and sells them through sales companies around the world.
entries.97dce5c9ca52a7a8: This business manufactures and sells household sewing machines. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥60,973 million, up 6.7% from the prior year (restated). The company explains that the increase was due to solid sales of entry-level and mid-range models in each region, the effect of pricing measures, and a positive impact from foreign exchange. The market for high-end models was sluggish due to inflation and the effects of U.S. tariff policy.
entries.986f12d5b7c3936a: This business manufactures and sells speed reducers and gears and also leases real estate, and it is carried out by the subsidiary Nissei Co., Ltd. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥21,441 million, up 7.1% from the prior year (restated). Including the effect of pricing measures, both speed reducers and gears were solid. Nissei became a consolidated subsidiary through a tender offer in January 2013 and became a wholly owned subsidiary in February 2022.
entries.ac01f816339132d2: A business that makes and sells industrial printing equipment used in factories and other settings. It consists of the Domino business in the United Kingdom and industrial printers, mainly garment printers. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥139,291 million, an increase of 1.5% from the prior year (after reclassification). Domino's consumables were firm and increased, while industrial printers declined significantly due to a deteriorating competitive environment in Europe and the Americas. This segment was newly established in the fiscal year ended March 2026, combining the business centered on garment printers, previously in the Machinery Business, with the Domino business. In March 2026, to strengthen the industrial printer business, the company made MUTOH Holdings Co., Ltd. (now MUTOH Co., Ltd.) a consolidated subsidiary through a tender offer.
entries.b860e47e3e623a29: Industrial equipment centered on machine tools. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥64,296 million, an increase of 35.9% from the prior year.
entries.c8cae1c8cf478dd7: A business centered on garment printers. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥13,964 million, a decrease of 22.0% from the prior year.
entries.ddd302aaab13f63c: A business that makes and sells printers, multifunction machines, label writers, label printers and scanners, and is the largest segment. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥570,583 million, an increase of 4.7% from the prior year (after reclassification). The company explains that laser multifunction machines and printers increased in each region as the supply constraints in the first half of the previous year reversed, inkjet multifunction machines generally grew in each region, and consumables were firm due to the effect of pricing measures. In labeling, both machines and consumables were firm in regions other than Europe. Foreign exchange also had a positive effect.
entries.ebe489ab548d0971: Label writers and label printers, and their consumables. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥72,235 million (up 4.2% from the prior year).
entries.f505854a46253e25: Industrial sewing machines used in sewing factories and other settings. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥18,673 million, a decrease of 6.6% from the prior year.
